[Documents and layout steps](v04-documents.html) built documents; this vignette
turns them into report files. A report is a document that is written to a file:
Word (DOCX), PDF, HTML or Markdown. The file says who made it and when, it
looks the same whoever opens it, and pubflow refuses to write it if it has a hole
in it. This vignette goes through

* what is added at render time and what is not part of the pipeline;
* the report spec, which sets up a format;
* failed steps in a report;
* the extras of Word files: header, footer, locks and the reference document;
* what each format needs, and the setup of PDF output.

It builds on pipeflow's vignette
[Error handling](https://rpahl.github.io/pipeflow/articles/v05c-error-handling.html)
for failed steps.

## Requirements

pubflow calls pandoc directly, so Word and PDF need the tools that pandoc and
its writers use. Which tools `pub_render()` needs depends on the format:

| Format | Needs |
|---|---|
| HTML, Markdown | nothing |
| Word (DOCX) | pandoc (>= 3.6) |
| PDF | pandoc and xelatex (the default) or Typst |

**pandoc** is found via the environment variable `PUBFLOW_PANDOC`, then
`RSTUDIO_PANDOC`, then the `PATH`.

**xelatex** is found on the `PATH` by pandoc. Tables need the LaTeX packages
of huxtable (`huxtable::install_latex_dependencies()`), and pubflow itself
needs pdflscape, fancyhdr, lastpage, float and newunicodechar. With TinyTeX:

```{r latex-packages, eval = FALSE}
tinytex::tlmgr_install(c("pdflscape", "fancyhdr", "lastpage", "float",
                         "newunicodechar"))
```

**Typst** is found via the environment variable `PUBFLOW_TYPST` (the
executable or its directory), then the `PATH`, then the typst that comes with
Quarto.

## The example

The document of the previous vignettes: a table and a figure of a linear model
of the ozone concentration. Its header and footer lines have the token
`{trace}`, which becomes the trace stamp of the report.

```{r doc}
library(pipeflow)
library(pubflow)
library(ggplot2)

fit <- lm(Ozone ~ Temp, data = airquality)
coefs <- data.frame(term = names(coef(fit)), estimate = unname(coef(fit)))

doc <- pub_doc(
    pub_section(
        "Results",
        pub_text(sprintf(
            "The model explains **%.0f%%** of the variance.",
            100 * summary(fit)$r.squared
        )),
        pub_table(
            coefs,
            caption = "Coefficients of the linear model",
            digits = c(estimate = 3L)
        ),
        pub_figure(
            ggplot(airquality, aes(Temp, Ozone)) + geom_point(na.rm = TRUE),
            caption = "Ozone by temperature",
            width = 6,
            height = 3.5
        )
    ),
    title = "Ozone in New York",
    meta = list(
        header = c(left = "Ozone study", right = "Draft"),
        footer = c(left = "{trace}")
    )
)
```

## Render-time metadata

Who rendered a report, when and with which application are facts about the act
of rendering. They are not part of the pipeline: if they were params of the
layout step, every render would outdate it. They are passed to `pub_render()`
instead, where they are merged over the metadata of the document:

```{r render}
file <- pub_render(
    doc,
    "docx",
    meta = list(author = "Jane Doe", app = "ozone-app", version = "1.2.0")
)
basename(file)
```

* The entries of `meta` win over those of the document, and `NULL` removes one.
* `time` is the render time, unless the document or `meta` sets one.
* The file name, the title block, the trace stamp, the front matter and the
  post-processors (below) all see the merged result.
* `pub_markdown()` and `pub_html()`, which the viewer uses, only see the
  metadata of the document, so what you see in the viewer doesn't change from
  one second to the next.

In an app, `meta` is where the user and the version go, e.g.
`list(author = session$user, app = "ozone-app", version = "1.2.0")`.

### Trace stamp

`pub_trace_stamp()` makes the line that `{trace}` stands for. It is an error
without an author, since pubflow doesn't guess it: on a server, the system user
is only the service account. Times are always UTC, with English month names:

```{r trace}
meta <- list(
    author = "Jane Doe",
    app = "ozone-app",
    version = "1.2.0",
    time = as.POSIXct("2026-11-02 09:30:00", tz = "UTC")
)
pub_trace_stamp(meta)
pub_trace_stamp(meta[c("author", "time")])
```

```{r trace-error, error = TRUE}
pub_trace_stamp(list(app = "ozone-app"))
```

### File names

Without `file`, the report goes to R's temporary directory under the name that
`pub_output_filename()` makes, the render time (UTC) and the title:

```{r filename}
pub_output_filename(list(title = "Ozone in New York", time = meta$time), "docx")
```

Call it yourself for a download name, e.g. in the `filename` of a Shiny
`downloadHandler()`.

## Report specs

A report spec sets up the report of one format, and `pub_render()` takes it as
`spec`. Without it, `pub_report_spec(format)` is used: all defaults. Printing a
spec shows what it uses:

```{r spec-print}
pub_report_spec("docx")
```

Every field acts in every format that can show it. A field that the format
can't use is an error, so a setting is never silently ignored:

```{r spec-error, error = TRUE}
pub_report_spec("docx", placeholder_color = "#0083c0")
```

The fields in short (`?pub_report_spec` has the details):

| Field | What it sets |
|---|---|
| `reference_docx`, `latex_preamble`, `typst_template` | The template of DOCX, of PDF via LaTeX, of PDF via Typst |
| `front_matter` | A function that returns what replaces the title block, e.g. a title page (default: the document's front matter) |
| `toc`, `toc_depth` | A table of contents after the front matter, and its depth |
| `number_sections` | Number the headings or not |
| `labels` | The words before the caption numbers |
| `page` | Paper size, orientation and margins (`pub_page()`) of DOCX and PDF |
| `figure` | Image format and resolution of figures |
| `placeholder_color` | Colour of placeholders in HTML and PDF |
| `lock` | Lock tables, figures, header and footer of DOCX files |
| `error_items` | Refuse or show failed steps |
| `post_process` | Functions that change the finished file |
| `pandoc_args` | Extra pandoc arguments |

### Title page, contents and page

The front matter replaces the title block. It is a function of the document
(with the render-time metadata) and the format that returns what a document can
hold: sections, outputs and lists of them. Its sections are not numbered, so the
numbers of the body start at 1. End it with a page break to start the contents
on a new page:

```{r spec-front}
title_page <- function(doc, format) {
    list(
        pub_text(paste("Prepared by", doc$meta$author)),
        pub_pagebreak()
    )
}

spec <- pub_report_spec(
    "pdf",
    front_matter = title_page,
    toc_depth = 2L,
    page = pub_page("letter", margins = c(left = 3)),
    labels = list(table = "Tab.", figure = "Fig.")
)
spec
```

The viewer doesn't show the front matter of a spec. A front matter that should
be previewed too belongs to the document: `pub_doc(front_matter = )` takes the
same outputs as the body and replaces the title block in the viewer and in every
format. The spec's function then is only needed for front matter of one format
(or with the render-time metadata); it replaces the document's and can build on
it with `doc$front_matter`:

```{r doc-front}
doc_front <- pub_doc(
    pub_section("Results", "Ozone peaks in July and August."),
    title = "Ozone report",
    front_matter = list(
        pub_section("Approval", "Signed by the analyst."),
        pub_pagebreak(),
        pub_toc()
    )
)
doc_front
```

A document that places `pub_toc()` itself (`what = "sections"`) gets no second
table of contents. Lists of figures and tables (`pub_toc(what = "figures")`)
don't count: to have only those, set `toc = FALSE` in the spec.

A spec is a plain list that is checked when it is used. To have one spec for
every format, write a function that builds them, so the front matter and the
labels are in one place:

```{r spec-variants}
my_spec <- function(format) {
    pub_report_spec(
        format,
        front_matter = title_page,
        labels = list(table = "Tab.", figure = "Fig.")
    )
}
spec_docx <- my_spec("docx")
```

Markdown shows the effect of a spec without any tool; the table caption now
starts with "Tab.":

```{r spec-md}
path <- pub_render(
    doc,
    "md",
    file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"),
    spec = my_spec("md"),
    meta = list(author = "Jane Doe")
)
grep("Tab\\.", readLines(path), value = TRUE)
```

## Failed steps in a report

A report has no holes: `pub_render()` refuses a document with error items and
lists the failed steps (see [Documents and layout steps](v04-documents.html)).
Run the pipeline of a report with the default `on_error = "stop"`, and a failed
step stops it before any document exists.

For a draft, run with `on_error = "continue"` and let the spec show the error
items instead:

```{r error-items}
pip <- pip_new("draft") |>
    pip_add("table", function() pub_table(head(airquality), caption = "Data")) |>
    pip_add("fit", function(data = airquality) lm(Ozone ~ Height, data = data)) |>
    pip_add(
        "report",
        function(table = ~ try(table), fit = ~ try(fit)) {
            pub_doc(pub_section("Results", table, fit), title = "Draft")
        }
    )
suppressWarnings(pip_run(pip, on_error = "continue", lgr = NULL))
draft <- pip[["report", "out"]]
```

```{r error-refuse, error = TRUE}
pub_render(draft, "md", file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"))
```

```{r error-show}
spec <- pub_report_spec("md", error_items = "show")
withCallingHandlers(
    pub_render(draft, "md", file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), spec = spec),
    pubflow_render_warning = function(w) {
        cat("Warning:", conditionMessage(w), "\n")
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
) |>
    invisible()
```

The file has an error box where the model of the failed step would be, and the
warning names the failed step. Use this for drafts only.

To check a document before rendering it, e.g. to tell the user of an app why a
report can't be downloaded yet, `pub_error_items()` lists its error items:

```{r error-list}
vapply(pub_error_items(draft), \(x) x$message, character(1))
```

## Word files

### Header, footer and locks

The Word file of the example above shows the header and footer lines of the
document, with `{trace}` expanded. They go into the header and footer part of
the reference document. A look into the file shows them:

```{r docx-text}
docx_text <- function(file, part) {
    dir <- tempfile()
    on.exit(unlink(dir, recursive = TRUE))
    utils::unzip(file, files = paste0("word/", part), exdir = dir)
    xml <- xml2::read_xml(file.path(dir, "word", part))
    xml2::xml_text(xml2::xml_find_all(xml, "//w:t"))
}
docx_text(file, "header1.xml")
docx_text(file, "footer1.xml")
```

The footer line at the left is the trace stamp, and "Page 1 / 1" is the
reference document's own page number. A footer line at the *right* replaces the
page number, as in PDF.

With `lock = TRUE` in the spec, the file also protects itself from accidental
editing: tables and figures are content controls that can't be deleted or
changed, and so are the whole header and the whole footer. An item opts out with
`pub_set_meta(locked = FALSE)`. By default, only the tables and figures with
`pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE)` are locked, and `lock = FALSE` locks nothing. The locks guard against
slips only, since Word lets users remove a lock in the control's properties. The
report you can rely on is the PDF.

### Post-processors

Two post-processors do the work above, `pub_pp_docx_header_footer()` and
`pub_pp_docx_lock()`. `pub_render()` adds the first to every DOCX report, the
second with `lock = TRUE`. Add them to the spec's `post_process` yourself to
give them arguments, e.g. other header lines than the document's, or a
different place in the order. Listing `pub_pp_docx_lock()` without `lock =
TRUE` locks the header and footer, but only the tables and figures with
`pub_set_meta(locked = TRUE)`.

Your own functions have the form `function(path, doc, spec)`. They change the
finished file in place, are called in order, and a failing one stops the render,
so no file is written. This one adds a note to a Markdown report:

```{r post-process}
add_note <- function(path, doc, spec) {
    writeLines(c(readLines(path), "", "<!-- checked -->"), path)
}
spec <- pub_report_spec("md", post_process = list(add_note))
path <- pub_render(doc, "md", file = tempfile(fileext = ".md"), spec = spec)
tail(readLines(path), 1L)
```

### The reference document

The look of a Word file comes from its reference document, pubflow's own
`system.file("templates", "reference.docx", package = "pubflow")` unless the
spec says `reference_docx`: A4, numbered headings, and a header and footer with
bookmarks for the lines. Start your own from a copy of it and change the
styles and the page in Word. The document must keep

* the styles in the table below (pandoc finds them by name; a missing one is
  added unformatted);
* the bookmarks of the header and footer lines that you use: `header_left`,
  `header_center`, `header_right`, `footer_left`, `footer_center` and
  `footer_right` (the last one surrounds "Page x / N"). A line without its
  bookmark is an error, so a stamp is never dropped unnoticed.

| Style | Type | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Heading 1 - Heading 5 | paragraph | numbered section headings (the numbering belongs to the styles) |
| Heading 1 Unnumbered - Heading 5 Unnumbered | paragraph | unnumbered sections (they keep the outline level, so they appear in the table of contents) |
| Item Title | paragraph | title line above an item |
| Table Caption, Image Caption | paragraph | numbered captions (before tables, after figures) |
| Figure | paragraph | the paragraph that holds an image |
| Placeholder | character | `[text]{.placeholder}` spans |
| Error | paragraph | error items (failed steps) |
| Title, Subtitle, Author, Date | paragraph | pandoc's title block |

The page setup, header and footer of the reference document apply to every
section, also to landscape pages. An explicit `page` in the spec overrides the
page of the reference document.

## PDF output

`pub_render()` takes the engine in `pdf_engine`:

```{r pdf, eval = FALSE}
pub_render(doc, "pdf", file = "ozone.pdf", meta = meta) # xelatex
pub_render(doc, "pdf", file = "ozone.pdf", meta = meta, pdf_engine = "typst")
```

To change the look of a PDF, use `latex_preamble` (a file that is included after
pubflow's own header, so it can load packages and change the page style) or
`typst_template` (start from `system.file("templates", "pubflow.typ", package =
"pubflow")`). A custom Typst template must write `$header-includes$` and the
title block, and take the lines of the header and footer from `$header-left$`
to `$footer-right$`.
